summary: The Federal Reserve places a currency order each year with the Treasury's printer.
realLife: The Federal Reserve Board orders each year's currency from the Treasury's Bureau of Engraving and Printing, sizing each denomination's order to expected demand and the notes expected to be destroyed.
sources: Federal Reserve Board, How does the Federal Reserve Board determine how much currency to order each year (page updated Dec 19, 2014): https://www.federalreserve.gov/faqs/how-does-the-federal-reserve-board-determine-how-much-currency-to-order-each-year.htm
inGame: the macro module's money records, read by the loading screen's progress step for the economy (loading-steps.economy).

turns.what: The year's order is cut because fewer notes are being destroyed or demanded.
turns.pulledBy: a falling cash demand in the macro model
turns.writesBack: a smaller order record the economy step can name

turns.what: The order grows only to replace worn notes.
turns.writesBack: an order sized to destroyed notes
